definition: A proof that a statement $P(n)$ holds for every positive integer $n$: show $P(1)$ is true, then show that $P(k)$ true implies $P(k + 1)$ true.
A proof that assumes the statement is false and deduces something impossible, so the statement must be true.
A particular case for which a statement is false, which shows that the statement is not always true.
A real number that cannot be written as $\frac{p}{q}$ with $p, q \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $q \ne 0$, such as $\sqrt{3}$ or $\pi$.
